subject: FastTrack pilot: latency & capacity recap
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@fasttrack-logistics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FastTrack pilot: latency & capacity recap

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed set of next steps so we can land on the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC).

Key signals from the call:
- Primary use case: real-time routing decisions for last-mile deliveries (sub-100ms desirable on per-request inference)
- Typical steady QPS: 250–400 requests/sec; peak bursts up to ~1,200 req/sec during regional batch windows (5–7 minutes)
- Response size: short LLM prompts (~30–120 tokens) for scoring/generation
- Compliance: standard SOC2 controls acceptable; considering VPC for upcoming procurement review

Initial recommendation (based on our experience):
- Hosted API pilot to validate model behavior and steady-state cost — we can support burstable traffic through autoscaling but sustained p95 < 100ms at 400 QPS will need a dedicated pool.
- If FastTrack requires sustained p95 < 50ms or consistent >800 QPS for production, Dedicated capacity is the safer path — predictable latency and reserved GPU pools.

Attachments included: pilot-qps-sla.xlsx (sample QPS profile + latency tradeoffs) and redwood-hosted-capacity-brief.pdf (short tradeoff doc). I also drafted a mutual action plan (MAP-FastTrack.md) with milestones.

Proposed next steps:
1) You share a week-long QPS sample (CSV or CloudWatch logs) that shows burst distribution — helps finalize sizing (Ben can run an offline throughput model).
2) Quick engineering call (30 min) this week for Ben to confirm KV-cache expectations and token lengths — available Thu/Fri.
3) We’ll scope a 2-week hosted pilot + optional dedicated-pooled benchmark if your procurement prefers a performance estimate for reserved capacity.

Please reply with which of the two windows below works for the eng call and whether you can send sample traffic by EOD Friday.

Windows (PST): Thu 10/22 9:00–10:30 or Fri 10/23 13:00–14:30

Thanks —

Subject: Re: FastTrack pilot: latency & capacity recap

Jordan / Elena —

Great notes. Quick follow-up from the SE side with some concrete thresholds to help decide Hosted vs Dedicated: 

Short answers:
- Sustained p95 <= 100ms at 400 QPS: likely fine on Hosted with recommended batching and prefix caching.
- Sustained p95 <= 50ms OR consistent >800 QPS: Dedicated (reserved GPUs) + optimized quantization recommended.
- Bursts to 1,200 for 5–7 minutes: Hosted autoscaling can absorb short bursts but may see transient p95 blips during cold scale. If those blips are unacceptable, a hybrid (Dedicated + Hosted fallback) is doable.

What I need from your team to size: pilot-qps-sla.xlsx has two tabs — steady week + burst day. Can you confirm token length distribution and whether you can accept ~200ms warm-up for the first request in a cold-batch scenario? Also, do you plan to keep models pinned (same version) during initial months? If yes, durable KV cache helps a lot.

If you prefer, I can run a simulated load for your traffic profile once you send the CSV — I’ll drop a short runbook with expected p95 numbers and the Dedicated capacity estimate.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: FastTrack pilot: latency & capacity recap

Thanks Jordan — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our engineering team: 

- Token lengths: most prompts are ~60 tokens; occasional longer prompts (200–250 tokens) for exception handling.
- Cold-warm behavior: some endpoints are latency-sensitive; we can tolerate up to 150–200ms cold penalty but not sustained >100ms p95.
- Model pinning: we intend to pin the model for the pilot (no rolling updates).

Sam and I will pull a 7-day QPS dump and a CSV of sample token lengths by EOD Thursday and upload to the Drive link you shared.

Also, procurement asked for a ballpark monthly committed cost for Dedicated vs Hosted for planning. Can you provide a back-of-envelope in the next 24 hours? If possible, include the cost delta for an assumed reserved pool that handles 800 steady QPS.

—Elena
Elena Ruiz
